best_plan.name: p7
best_plan.rationale: p7 gives the best overall cost-quality trade-off. It keeps the cheap exact filter on idx to isolate reviews for taken_3, then uses a lightweight semantic filter with a better-calibrated prompt for net favorable reviews. Across runs it matched p1's low cost closely while achieving better observed accuracy on average, including one perfect run, so the small extra cost is justified by the improved quality.

plan_codes.p1:
pipeline = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name, "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
pipeline.filter(lambda row: str(row["idx"]).strip().lower() == "taken_3")
pipeline.sem_filter(
    "the review text expresses an overall positive opinion of the movie",
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE,
    depends_on=["reviewText"]
)
pipeline.groupby([], ["count"], ["reviewId"])
pipeline.project(["count(reviewId)"])
pipeline

plan_codes.p4:
pipeline = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name, "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
pipeline.filter(lambda row: str(row["idx"]).strip().lower() == "taken_3")
pipeline.sem_map(
    [
        {"name": "sentiment_label", "type": str, "description": "Overall review sentiment toward the movie: positive, mixed, neutral, or negative."},
        {"name": "is_clearly_positive", "type": bool, "description": "True only if the review is clearly overall positive or favorable, not mixed, neutral, sarcastic, or negative."}
    ],
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE
)
pipeline.filter(lambda row: str(row["sentiment_label"]).strip().lower() == "positive" and bool(row["is_clearly_positive"]) is True)
pipeline.groupby([], ["count"], ["reviewId"])
pipeline.project(["count(reviewId)"])
pipeline
